message:
fix(deploy): a re-publish was overwriting its own rollback point

Found while preparing the 0.2.109 recovery, which is exactly this case: a revision
of a version that is already published.

backup_current_pair named the backup after the published version alone. That is
right once. A second run -- a retry after a partial failure, which this script
otherwise encourages by being idempotent -- computes the same name again and
copies over it, replacing the rollback point with the thing you would be rolling
back FROM. The idempotence that makes re-running safe everywhere else is what
made it unsafe here. An existing backup is now never written over; the new one
gets a timestamped name.

Negative control: with the guard removed, the new cases fail and the backup is
observed turning into the new manifest.

Also: a dry run always exited 1. It uploads nothing, so anything new still 404s,
and the external check counted that as failure. An exit code that is always 1
stops being a signal, so a dry run now skips the external check and says it
skipped it.

And a limitation removed rather than restated. Until now the C++ side of a release
was only checked against a FIXTURE signed with the release key -- which proves the
compiled-in key accepts that key's signatures, not that the product accepts the
document being published. remote60_verify_release runs the shipped load_manifest()
and default_verifier() against a real manifest, and flips a byte to show it is
actually looking. Run here on the document before publishing and again on the
bytes pulled back off the server afterwards.
